newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Fed's Rivlin says Americans need to save more.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Fed's Rivlin says Americans need to save more.

text.p: If the United States is to have the highest sustainable growth in its economy and productivity 30 years from now, Americans need to save more, Federal Reserve Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin said Friday.
She spoke at a Society of Government Economists conference on "Far out Federal fiscal policy: getting ready for 2025."
"The fundamental challenge to American society ... is a growth challenge," Rivlin said. And one question is 'What fiscal policy will get us on the highest sustainable growth path?'" she added.
Fiscal options should be judged by how they will likely increase national saving, Rivlin said.
She expressed skepticism about the idea of using widespread tax cuts to boost economic growth.
"I am a skeptic of the magic of across-the-board tax cuts with respect to increasing growth," she said.
